'''Shelley D. Minteer''' (born 1975) is an American academic and chemistry professor at the [[University of Utah]]. Minteer field of study focuses on the interface between [[biocatalysts]] and enzyme-based electrodes for biofuel cells and sensors.

== Education and early career ==
Minteer received a bachelor's in chemistry from [[Western Illinois University]] in 1995<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://chem.utah.edu/directory/minteer/|title=Shelley D. Minteer - Department of Chemistry - The University of Utah|website=chem.utah.edu|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=ACS Sensors|doi=10.1021/acssensors.8b00017|doi-access=free}}</ref> and earned her doctorate under the supervision of [[Johna Leddy]] from the [[University of Iowa]] in 2000.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chem.uiowa.edu/leddy-lab/group-members|title=Group Members {{!}} Leddy Lab {{!}} Department of Chemistry {{!}} College of Liberal Arts and Sciences {{!}} The University of Iowa|website=chem.uiowa.edu|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref> In 2000, Minteer joined [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]] as an assistant professor.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Minteer|first1=Shelley D.|last2=Moehlenbrock|first2=Michael J.|date=2008-05-22|title=Extended lifetime biofuel cells|journal=Chemical Society Reviews|language=en|volume=37|issue=6|pages=1188–1196|doi=10.1039/B708013C|pmid=18497931|issn=1460-4744}}</ref> While there she joined the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] (AIChE) education academy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aiche.org/proceedings/people/shelley-d-minteer|title=Shelley D. Minteer {{!}} AIChE Academy|website=www.aiche.org|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref> At [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]], Minteer worked on several inventions, including [[drug delivery]] systems, enzymes, and novel electrodes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/shelley-d-minteer|title=Shelley D. Minteer Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search|website=patents.justia.com|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref> She developed enzyme immobilization membranes to improve the stability of biosensor and biofuel electrodes.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.stlacs.org/awards/st-louis-award/dr-shelley-d-minteer-2008-st-louis-award-winner/|title=St. Louis Section–American Chemical Society » Dr. Shelley D Minteer: 2008 St. Louis Award Winner|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meredith|first1=Matthew T.|last2=Minteer|first2=Shelley D.|date=2012|title=Biofuel Cells: Enhanced Enzymatic Bioelectrocatalysis|journal=Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry|volume=5|issue=1|pages=157–179|doi=10.1146/annurev-anchem-062011-143049|pmid=22524222|bibcode=2012ARAC....5..157M}}</ref> In 2003 Minteer and her graduate student Nick Akers co-founded ''Akermin'' to commercialise their work on [[Mitochondrion|mitochondria]]-based biofuel cells.<ref name=":1" /> She was made a full professor at [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=D. Minteer|first1=S.|last2=Martin|first2=G.|last3=Lau|first3=C.|last4=Svoboda|first4=V.|last5=J. Cooney|first5=M.|date=2008|title=Enzyme catalysed biofuel cells|journal=Energy & Environmental Science|language=en|volume=1|issue=3|pages=320–337|doi=10.1039/B809009B}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Minteer worked at [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]] for eleven years before joining the [[University of Utah]] in 2011.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cai|first1=Rong|last2=Minteer|first2=Shelley D.|date=2018-11-09|title=Nitrogenase Bioelectrocatalysis: From Understanding Electron-Transfer Mechanisms to Energy Applications|journal=ACS Energy Letters|volume=3|issue=11|pages=2736–2742|doi=10.1021/acsenergylett.8b01637|doi-access=free}}</ref> She studies the interface between [[biocatalysts]] and [[electrode]] surfaces for [[Electrocatalyst|bioelectrocatalysis]].<ref name=":0" /> She works on [[enzyme cascade]]s for bioelectrocatalysis as well as [[organelle]] bioelectrocatalysis for detection of microscopic events. She also works on the production of biofuels, using [[synthetic biology]] and nanotechnology to improve the production.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/ecs1902/docs/227_final_program_e1654c28867612|title=227th ECS Meeting: Meeting Program|website=Issuu|language=en|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref> Minteer became interested in extending the lifetimes of fuels and improving the efficiency of oxidation.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Minteer|first1=Shelley D|last2=Liaw|first2=Bor Yann|last3=Cooney|first3=Michael J|date=2007|title=Enzyme-based biofuel cells|journal=Current Opinion in Biotechnology|language=en|volume=18|issue=3|pages=228–234|doi=10.1016/j.copbio.2007.03.007|pmid=17399977}}</ref> She demonstrated the first room temperature enzyme-based [[fuel cell]]s in 2014.<ref name="Member Spotlight - Shelley Minteer">{{Cite web|url=https://www.electrochem.org/redcat-blog/member-spotlight-shelley-minteer/|title=Member Spotlight - Shelley Minteer|date=2014-11-05|website=ECS|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref> The fuel cells use [[JP-8]], a [[kerosene]] based fuel cells used by the [[United States Armed Forces]], as well as enzymes as catalysts to oxidise the [[JP-8]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.unews.utah.edu/news_releases/jet-fueled-electricity-at-room-temperature/|title=Jet-Fueled Electricity at Room Temperature {{!}} University of Utah News|website=archive.unews.utah.edu|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref>

She was the first to demonstrate paper-based batteries using an electrode coated in bacteria.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/engineers-create-collapsible-battery-powered-help-dirty-water|title=Engineers create collapsible battery powered with the help of dirty water|date=2015-06-27|website=PBS NewsHour|language=en-us|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Grete Eliassen|title=Bio-Inspired Batteries with guest researcher Shelley D. Minteer, Ph.D.|date=2012-07-16|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EcbxPAjexfQ|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref> The batteries can be used to power biosensors and sensor networks.<ref name=":4" /> Minteer looks to bioengineer natural [[metabolic pathway]]s for bioanodes in [[biofuel]] cells and the discovery of enzymes. In 2015 Minteer joined the [[Joint Center for Energy Storage Research]] to help take more rational design for redox flow batteries.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=http://www.jcesr.org/about/leadership/research-leadership/shelley-minteer-2/|title=Shelley Minteer - Joint Center for Energy Storage Research|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref> Her efforts include the development of electroanalytical and spectroscopic assays to determine [[quantitative structure–activity relationship]] modelling.<ref name=":5" /> She works on electrolytes that minimise crossover and more soluble electrolytes.<ref name=":5" /> Minteer worked with Brett Helms at [[University of California, Berkeley]] on electroanalytical tools to study [[oligomer]] electrolytes.<ref name=":5" />

Minteer is an associate editor of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'', having previously served as an editor of the ''[[Journal of the Electrochemical Society]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/jacsat/editors.html|title=Editors|website=pubs.acs.org|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.coe.utah.edu/2013/02/15/ustar-professor-appointed-technical-editor-of-ecs-journals/|title=USTAR Professor Appointed Technical Editor of ECS Journals|date=2013-02-15|website=The College of Engineering at the University of Utah|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref>

* 2018 [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] Fellow<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Science|first=American Association for the Advancement of|date=2018-11-30|title=2018 AAAS Fellows approved by the AAAS Council|journal=Science|language=en|volume=362|issue=6418|pages=1010–1013|doi=10.1126/science.362.6418.1010|bibcode=2018Sci...362.1010.|issn=0036-8075|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/elections/AAAS-names-2018-Fellows/96/web/2018/12|title=AAAS names 2018 Fellows|website=Chemical & Engineering News|language=en|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref>

* 2010 [[International Society of Electrochemistry]] Tajima Prize<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ise-online.org/awards/taj.php|title=International Society of Electrochemistry|website=www.ise-online.org|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref>
* 2008 [[American Chemical Society]] St. Louis Award<ref name=":1" />
* 2008 [[Scientific American]] Top 50<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/scientific-american-50-sa-2006-12/|title=Scientific American 50: SA 50 Winners and Contributors|website=Scientific American|language=en|access-date=2019-04-13}}</ref>
* 2008 [[Society of Electroanalytical Chemists]] Young Investigator Award<ref name=":2" />
* 2006 [[United States Department of Defense]] Okaloosa Award<ref name=":0" />
